head.hi: The Van Velsor. The Maternal Side.

body.p: The poets''s mother, Louisa Van Velsor, ‸born Sept. 22, 1795, was of Dutch descent, her δancestors, a race of sea folks and mariners. being genuine Hollanders. The Van Velsors were also passionately fond of books,horses and Louisa, when a girl, was a daring and spirited rider. As a woman, she was‸inof sof marked spiritual and intuitive nature, yet healthy and strong, possessed of a kind and generous heart, and good sense, , she wasand cheerful and equable in temper.

Walt Whitman himself makes much of the women of his live and family. Both his grandmothers, who were very fond of him, (and he was with ‸one of the other of them ‸part of every year, untill he was quite a grownbig lad) appear to have been goodnoble and endearing character. He speaksAt the death of his own mother ‸he spoke of her and his sister Martha, and the two grandmothers ‸alluded to, alluded to as by for "the best and sweetest women I ever saw, or ever expect to see."

Like the Whitmans the Van Velsors too were farmers on their own land. Though both families were well -to-do for those times, the biblical prayer for "neither poverty nor riches" might have been considered fulfilled in either case. The poet's father died in Brooklyn New York July 11, 1855. The "dear dear mother" in Camden, New jersey, may 23, 1873.
